main_body: Snow-covered log cabin: a large snow-covered roof slope (rows ~8-34) above a log-wall front with a central wooden door and two lit windows (rows ~38-62)
top_band: Pale white/light-blue snow roof, rows ~8-34, a large lit slope with a thicker lighter eave band at rows ~31-35, then icicles and a dark eave shadow at rows ~36-39
evidence: In a column through the middle, the snow roof reads as a tall light roof surface (rows 8-34) ending in a bright snow lip at the eave. Below it, icicles and a dark shadow row (36-39) sit above the log wall, door and windows (rows 40-62). The windows have dark blue shutters and inset frames, and the door has iron straps and a dark edge. The roof is a large top-slope surface, not a thin rim, which matches the stall roofs in the reference. It has no receding side faces and the front reads as a vertical wall. It passes as 3/4.

style.evidence: The snow roof has about 5 steps (white, pale blue, mid blue-grey, shadow blue and dark scallops), with dotted drift marks and icicles. The log wall carries 4-5 browns and the windows have a gradient of warm yellows and oranges. Outlines are dark brown on the wood and dark blue-grey on the snow, so they carry material tint, not black. The large snow areas are broad near-flat whites (the upper roof and the large pale expanse around rows 10-30) with only sparse speckles, so there are some flat fills of at least 5x5 px. Detail density is a little below the tile-roof reference, which has per-tile highlights across the whole roof. It is acceptable next to it but slightly thinner in the roof area.
